title: Wasserstein Distributional Learning
testbed_rationale: The paper focuses on general statistical density-on-scalar regression methodology using aggregated 1D global land temperature anomaly distributions rather than spatial climate model parameterization or physical process simulation testbeds.
pain_points: Inherent non-negativity and unit-integral constraints of probability density functions in functional regression
Non-convexity and noisy loss gradients when optimizing the Wasserstein loss directly over mixture model parameters
Computational scaling and non-crossing quantile function constraints in existing methods such as Fréchet regression
Handling sparse empirical quantiles where continuous density estimates are not directly available
extraction_notes: The primary ML methodological innovation is Wasserstein Distributional Learning (WDL) using Semi-parametric Conditional Gaussian Mixture Models (SCGMM) optimized with boosted trees via Majorization-Minimization. The climate application predicts the annual empirical distribution of daily global mean land temperature anomalies from atmospheric forcings and ENSO.
